description: Fixed-length throughput measurement of an OpenAI-compatible streaming chat endpoint. Two workloads run serially in each pass: prefill.in2048.out1 (about 2048 prompt tokens, one output token; prefill time is the client time from dispatch to the first output chunk) and decode.in128.out256 (about 128 prompt tokens, exactly 256 output tokens; decode throughput is N-1 tokens divided by the first-to-last chunk interval, and is not obtained when the engine sends fewer than 0.9 chunks per token). Prompt sizes are calibrated with the engine's own usage counts. Every prompt begins with a unique nonce so no prefix can be reused, and reported cached prompt tokens must be zero. A request counts only if it reaches its input and output lengths; a pass with any request that does not is excluded from the metrics and stays in the repetitions. All intervals come from one monotonic clock at the client. Warm-up and formal pass counts come from the experiment contract (--warmup, --repetitions). Cold load is not measured. Peak memory is sampled only when --memory-pid is given, and swap-out is the whole-machine delta on a loopback endpoint. It does not judge output quality or API conformance; run engine-api-conformance first, with thinking disabled for reasoning models. Before every run the driver repeats its negative control: a reference engine with known rates that the timing must recover, a slower one that must read slower, and injected faults (reported cache hits, short output, missing usage, coalesced chunks, HTTP errors) that must each be caught.

harness.reason: The driver script sends HTTP requests to the endpoint directly; no agent harness is involved.

dataset.reason: The prompts are built by the scripts from a fixed word list and a fixed seed; there is no external dataset.

cache_policy: No prefix reuse: a unique nonce starts every prompt, including warm-up and calibration prompts, and reported cached prompt tokens must be zero. Engines that do not report cached tokens are recorded as unverified.
